questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the radiations X and Y and state how each can be detected. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The electromagnetic spectrum in order of **decreasing wavelength** is: radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, **ultraviolet**, **X-rays**, gamma rays. Between visible light and gamma rays we therefore find:

- **X = ultraviolet (UV) radiation.** It is detected by a **fluorescent material** (a fluorescent paper or the security mark on a banknote glows when UV falls on it), by **photographic film** or by a UV-sensitive photocell.
- **Y = X-rays.** They are detected by **photographic film or plate** (it becomes darker where X-rays fall), by a **fluorescent screen** (it glows) or by a Geiger-Muller tube.

questions.enonce_markdown: Give two differences between electromagnetic waves and sound waves. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Electromagnetic waves | Sound waves |
|---|---|
| **Transverse** waves | **Longitudinal** waves |
| Can travel through a **vacuum** (no medium needed) | **Need a material medium** (solid, liquid or gas); cannot travel in a vacuum |
| Speed in air or vacuum is very large, $3.0\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ | Speed in air is much smaller, about $340\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ |

(Any two of these differences.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Differentiate between transverse and longitudinal waves. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a **transverse wave** the particles of the medium (or the electric and magnetic fields) vibrate **at right angles (perpendicular)** to the direction in which the wave travels (for example water waves, light).

In a **longitudinal wave** the particles vibrate **parallel** to the direction of travel of the wave, forming compressions and rarefactions (for example sound).
